chunks.arabic_text: رِجَالُ الْكَشِّيِّ: مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ قُلْوَيْهَ وَالْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ الْحَسَنِ بْنِ بَنْدَارٍ الْقُمِّيُّ، عَنْ سَعْدِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ مَهْزَارٍ وَمُحْمَدِ بْنِ عِيسَى بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ، عَنْ عَلِيِّ بْنِ مَهْزَارٍ قَالَ

translations.en: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Qulawayh and al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Bundar al-Qummi, from Sa'd ibn Abdallah, from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar and Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said:

chunks.arabic_text: سَمِعْتُ أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ يَقُولُ وَقدْ ذُكِرَ عِنْدَهُ أَبُو الْخَطَّابِ: لَعَنَ اللَّهُ أَبَا الْخَطَّابِ وَلَعَنَ أَصْحَابَهُ وَلَعَنَ الشَّاكِّينَ فِي لَعْنِهِ وَلَعَنَ مَنْ قَدِمَ فِي ذَلِكَ وَشُكَّ فِيهِ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: هَذَا أَبُو الْغَمْرِ وَجَعْفَرُ بْنُ وَاقِدٍ وَهَاشِمُ بْنُ أَبِي هَاشِمٍ اسْتَأْكَلُوا بِنَا النَّاسَ وَصَارُوا دُعَاةً يَدْعُونَ النَّاسَ إِلَى مَا دُعِيَ إِلَيْهِ أَبُو الْخَطَّابِ، لَعَنَهُ اللَّهُ وَلَعَنَهُمْ مَعَهُ وَلَعَنَ مَنْ قَبِلَ ذَلِكَ مِنْهُمْ، يَا عَلِيُّ لَا تَتَحَرَّجَنَّ مِنْ لَعْنِهِمْ لَعَنَهُمُ اللَّهُ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ قَدْ لَعَنَهُمْ، ثُمَّ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَآلِهِ وَسَلَّمَ: مَنْ تَأَثَّمَ أَنْ يَلْعَنَ مَنْ لَعَنَهُ اللَّهُ فَعَلَيْهِ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ

translations.en: I heard Aba Ja'far (peace be upon him) say when Abu al-Khattab was mentioned in his presence: May Allah curse Abu al-Khattab, curse his companions, curse those who question his cursing, and curse those who abstain from doing it doubting its propriety. Then he said: Here are Abu al-Ghamr, Ja'far ibn Waqid and Hashim ibn Abi Hashim! They have used us to take wealth from the people and have become callers calling the people to what Abu al-Khattab used to call to! May Allah curse him and curse them with him, may He curse whoever accepts that from them. O Ali – do not feel any discomfort in cursing them – may Allah curse them – for they have been cursed by Allah. Then he said: the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever refrains from cursing the one who is cursed by Allah considering it a sin then upon him be the curse of Allah.

en.summary: Imam al-Jawad (peace be upon him) pronounces a curse upon Abu al-Khattab and his followers, specifically naming Abu al-Ghamr, Ja'far ibn Waqid, and Hashim ibn Abi Hashim, who exploited his name to collect wealth and propagated his teachings. He instructs Ali to not hesitate in cursing them, affirming that Allah has already cursed them, and cites the Prophet's saying that withholding a curse on the divinely cursed is itself a sin. This narration highlights the concept of *al-raj'ah* (return) and the specific status of these figures in Shia eschatology, where their return is a sign of the reappearance of Imam al-Mahdi.
en.seo_question: Who are the specific companions mentioned as followers of Abu al-Khattab and why were they cursed?

key_terms.أبو الخطاب: Abu al-Khattab, a prominent early Shia figure whose teachings were later scrutinized
key_terms.استأكلوا بنا الناس: They used us to take wealth from the people, referring to collecting khums or donations in the Imam's name
key_terms.دعاة: Callers/proponents, those who invite others to a specific belief or practice
key_terms.لا تتحرجن: Do not feel discomfort or hesitation
key_terms.تأثم: Consider it a sin or feel guilty
